rationale: MandarinX currently lists Level 1 among courses that can be audited for free. The six-week beginner path focuses on tones, everyday spoken vocabulary and practical communication, offering a self-paced English-mediated alternative to the current BLCU cohort route. Paid verified-track extras and certification are kept separate from the F2 learning-access classification.

The freely accessible course contains more than 90 sequenced grammar and morphology lessons with audio-supported examples and interactive marked exercises. Learners who cannot yet read Arabic are explicitly directed to a separate free reading course first. Its depth makes it a credible Modern Standard Arabic specialist challenger, while its grammar-heavy balance and Classical/Qur'anic framing remain deep-review considerations.

Al Jazeera explicitly describes the site as a free open educational source. The General Language area spans introductory, beginner, elementary, intermediate, upper-intermediate, advanced and proficiency material, including a full Arabic letters-and-sounds sequence, daily-life lessons, grammar series, interactive exercise results and placement testing. It is non-linear rather than a fixed course, but the project covers high-quality open learning experiences as well as courses, so it merits deep comparison as a broad free Arabic pathway.
